source.text: וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אָהַ֞ב נָשִׁ֧ים נָכְרִיּ֛וֹת רַבּ֖וֹת וְאֶת־בַּת־פַּרְעֹ֑ה מוֹאֲבִיּ֤וֹת עַמֳּנִיּוֹת֙ אֲדֹ֣מִיֹּ֔ת צֵדְנִיֹּ֖ת חִתִּיֹּֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And the king Solomon loved women foreign many, and [the] daughter of Pharaoh, Moabite [women], Ammonite [women], Edomite [women], Sidonian [women], Hittite [women],

en.L: And King Solomon loved many foreign women, along with the daughter of Pharaoh: Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, [and] Hittite [women],
en.B: King Solomon loved many foreign women besides Pharaoh's daughter: women of Moab, Ammon, Edom, Sidon, and the Hittites,
en.R: King Solomon loved many women from other nations. Besides Pharaoh's daughter, he loved women from Moab, Ammon, Edom, Sidon, and the land of the Hittites.

decisions.choice: loved: desire and attachment, here for women of other nations
decisions.reason: The same verb said that "Solomon loved Yahweh" (3:3). Now his love goes to many foreign women. The writer sets the two loves side by side: the divided love of verse 4 begins here.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Pharaoh: a marriage that sealed an alliance
decisions.reason: Solomon's marriage to the daughter of the king of Egypt was told at 3:1 (also 7:8; 9:16, 24). Kings married the daughters of other kings to bind treaties, and the nations listed here were Israel's neighbors.

decisions.choice: many foreign women: what the law warned the king against
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy tells the king not to take many wives, "so that his heart does not turn away" (Deuteronomy 17:17). Verses 3-4 use the same words for what happened to Solomon.

decisions.choice: [women] (Literal); women of Moab ... (Balanced); women from Moab ... (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses feminine forms of the nation names, which mean women of those peoples. English needs the noun; Balanced and Readable name the lands.

source.text: מִן־הַגּוֹיִ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽמַר־יְהוָה֩ אֶל־בְּנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל לֹֽא־תָבֹ֣אוּ בָהֶ֗ם וְהֵם֙ לֹא־יָבֹ֣אוּ בָכֶ֔ם אָכֵן֙ יַטּ֣וּ אֶת־לְבַבְכֶ֔ם אַחֲרֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם בָּהֶ֛ם דָּבַ֥ק שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְאַהֲבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: from the nations which had said Yahweh to [the] sons of Israel, Not you shall go in among them, and they not shall go in among you; surely they will turn your heart after their gods. To them clung Solomon in love.

en.L: from the nations of which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, "You shall not go in among them, and they shall not go in among you; surely they will turn your heart after their gods." To these Solomon clung in love.
en.B: from the nations {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had warned the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} about: "Do not intermarry with them, and do not let them intermarry with you, for they will surely turn your hearts to follow their gods." Yet Solomon held fast to these women in love.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had told the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} not to marry people from these nations. He had said, "Do not marry them, and do not let them marry you. They will certainly lead you to worship their gods." But Solomon held on to these women and loved them.

decisions.choice: go in among them: marry into them
decisions.reason: To "go in" to a people, and they to you, means to marry and become one family with them, as the parallel laws say outright (Deuteronomy 7:3).

decisions.choice: the words the LORD had said: the law of Exodus and Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: The quotation sums up Exodus 34:15-16 and Deuteronomy 7:3-4, which forbid marriage with the peoples of Canaan because they would turn Israel to their gods. The writer applies the same reason to Solomon's wives from neighboring nations.

decisions.choice: clung: held fast with loyal attachment
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a man holding fast to his wife (Genesis 2:24) and, often, of Israel holding fast to Yahweh (Deuteronomy 10:20; 11:22; 13:5). Solomon gives the loyalty he owed to Yahweh to these women.

decisions.choice: intermarry (Balanced); marry (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what the idiom means (m1); Literal keeps "go in among".

source.text: וַיְהִי־ל֣וֹ נָשִׁ֗ים שָׂרוֹת֙ שְׁבַ֣ע מֵא֔וֹת וּפִֽלַגְשִׁ֖ים שְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֑וֹת וַיַּטּ֥וּ נָשָׁ֖יו אֶת־לִבּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And were to him wives, princesses, seven hundred, and concubines three hundred; and turned his wives his heart.

en.L: And he had 700 wives, princesses, and 300 concubines; and his wives turned his heart away.
en.B: He had 700 wives of royal birth and 300 concubines, and his wives turned his heart away.
en.R: He had 700 wives who were princesses, and 300 concubines (secondary wives). His wives turned his heart away.

decisions.choice: princesses: wives from royal and noble families
decisions.reason: The word is the feminine of the word for a prince or official. These were wives of high birth, many of them daughters of foreign kings and chiefs given in marriage to seal alliances.

decisions.choice: concubines: wives of lower rank
decisions.reason: A concubine was a lawful partner of a man, but without the full standing of a wife; her children did not inherit in the same way (Genesis 25:6). A great household of wives was a sign of a king's wealth and power (Song of Songs 6:8).

decisions.choice: his wives turned his heart: the result the law foresaw
decisions.reason: The clause takes up the warning quoted in verse 2 and the law for kings (Deuteronomy 17:17), and verse 4 repeats it. The numbers stress how far Solomon went beyond what the law allowed.
Numbers above ninety-nine are written as numerals.

decisions.choice: concubines (secondary wives)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word the first time it appears in the chapter, as in Judges.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י לְעֵת֙ זִקְנַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה נָשָׁיו֙ הִטּ֣וּ אֶת־לְבָב֔וֹ אַחֲרֵ֖י אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וְלֹא־הָיָ֨ה לְבָב֤וֹ שָׁלֵם֙ עִם־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔יו כִּלְבַ֖ב דָּוִ֥יד אָבִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was at [the] time of [the] old age of Solomon, his wives turned his heart after gods other, and not was his heart complete with Yahweh his God as [the] heart of David his father.

en.L: And it happened at the time of Solomon's old age [that] his wives turned his heart after other gods, and his heart was not whole with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God, as the heart of David his father [had been].
en.B: When Solomon was old, his wives turned his heart to follow other gods, and his heart was not wholly devoted to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God, as the heart of his father David had been.
en.R: As Solomon grew old, his wives led him to worship other gods. He was no longer completely loyal to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God, as his father David had been.

decisions.choice: whole: undivided, fully loyal
decisions.reason: The word means complete or at peace. A heart that is whole with Yahweh is wholly given to him, with no other loyalty beside his (8:61; 15:3, 14).

decisions.choice: as the heart of David: David as the standard for the kings
decisions.reason: David sinned gravely (15:5), but he never served other gods. Kings measures each king of his line by this loyalty (15:3, 11; 2 Kings 18:3).

decisions.choice: at the time of Solomon's old age: the turning came late
decisions.reason: The writer places Solomon's worship of other gods in the last part of his reign, after the temple and the years of blessing in chapters 3-10.

decisions.choice: led him to worship other gods
decisions.reason: Readable says what turning the heart after other gods meant in practice.

source.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֣י עַשְׁתֹּ֔רֶת אֱלֹהֵ֖י צִדֹנִ֑ים וְאַחֲרֵ֣י מִלְכֹּ֔ם שִׁקֻּ֖ץ עַמֹּנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Solomon after Ashtoreth [the] god of [the] Sidonians, and after Milcom [the] detestable thing of [the] Ammonites.

en.L: And Solomon went after Ashtoreth the god of the Sidonians, and after Milcom the detestable thing of the Ammonites.
en.B: Solomon followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians and Milcom the detestable god of the Ammonites.
en.R: Solomon worshiped Ashtoreth, the goddess of the people of Sidon, and Milcom, the disgusting god of the Ammonites.

decisions.choice: went after: followed in worship
decisions.reason: To go after a god is to follow and serve it, as a servant follows a master (Deuteronomy 6:14; 8:19).

decisions.choice: Ashtoreth: the Canaanite goddess Astarte
decisions.reason: Ashtoreth was a goddess of fertility and war, worshiped in Sidon and across Canaan (Judges 2:13; 1 Samuel 7:3; 31:10). The Hebrew word for "god" here serves for a goddess too, since Hebrew has no separate word. The vowels of her name may have been given those of the word for "shame", as was sometimes done with the names of foreign gods.

decisions.choice: the detestable thing: a scornful name for a foreign god
decisions.reason: The word means something loathsome and is used most often of idols and the gods of the nations (Deuteronomy 29:16; 2 Kings 23:13). The writer does not give Milcom the title "god" but calls him what he is in Yahweh's eyes.

decisions.choice: Milcom: the national god of Ammon
decisions.reason: The name comes from the word for "king". The same letters stand in 2 Samuel 12:30, where the crown of the Ammonites' "king" may be the crown of Milcom.

decisions.choice: goddess
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "goddess", since Ashtoreth was female (m2). Literal keeps "god", as the Hebrew has.

decisions.choice: the detestable thing (Literal); the detestable god (Balanced); the disgusting god (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "god" so that the reader knows what kind of thing is meant; Readable says "disgusting", as Deuteronomy 29:16 does.

source.text: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹ֥א מִלֵּ֛א אַחֲרֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה כְּדָוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And did Solomon the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and not he fully followed after Yahweh as David his father.

en.L: And Solomon did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and did not fully follow {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as David his father [did].
en.B: So Solomon did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and did not follow {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} wholeheartedly, as his father David had done.
en.R: Solomon did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. He did not follow {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} completely, as his father David had done.

decisions.choice: fully follow: follow with complete loyalty
decisions.reason: The phrase is literally "fill after": to go after Yahweh with nothing held back. It is said of Caleb and Joshua (Numbers 14:24; 32:11-12; Deuteronomy 1:36).

decisions.choice: did the evil in the eyes of Yahweh: the verdict on a king
decisions.reason: This is the first time Kings passes its standard verdict on a king. Yahweh's judgment, not the king's success, is the measure, as in Judges (Judges 2:11).

decisions.choice: did the evil in [the] eyes of / did what was evil in the sight of / did what the LORD said was evil
decisions.reason: The verdict formula is worded the same way at each level in these books.

source.text: אָז֩ יִבְנֶ֨ה שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה בָּמָ֗ה לִכְמוֹשׁ֙ שִׁקֻּ֣ץ מוֹאָ֔ב בָּהָ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וּלְמֹ֕לֶךְ שִׁקֻּ֖ץ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Then built Solomon a high place for Chemosh [the] detestable thing of Moab, on the mountain which [is] before Jerusalem, and for Molech [the] detestable thing of [the] sons of Ammon.

en.L: Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh the detestable thing of Moab, on the mountain that [is] east of Jerusalem, and for Molech the detestable thing of the sons of Ammon.
en.B: At that time Solomon built a high place for Chemosh the detestable god of Moab on the hill east of Jerusalem, and one for Molech the detestable god of the Ammonites.
en.R: On the hill east of Jerusalem, Solomon built a hilltop shrine for Chemosh, the disgusting god of Moab. He also built one for Molech, the disgusting god of the Ammonites.

decisions.choice: before Jerusalem: east of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The front was the east for someone facing the sunrise. The hill is the ridge east of the city, the Mount of Olives; 2 Kings 23:13 calls it the Mount of Destruction when Josiah tears down these shrines.

decisions.choice: Chemosh: the god of Moab
decisions.reason: Chemosh was Moab's national god (Numbers 21:29; Judges 11:24).

decisions.choice: Molech: the god of the Ammonites, linked with child sacrifice
decisions.reason: The law forbids giving children to Molech (Leviticus 18:21; 20:2-5). Verses 5 and 33 name Milcom as the god of Ammon, and both names come from the word for "king", so Molech may be another form of the name Milcom. Some ancient Greek manuscripts read "their king" here.

decisions.choice: a high place: a shrine with an altar
decisions.reason: As at 3:2, a high place was a place of worship, often on raised ground. These ones were built for foreign gods, in sight of the temple.

decisions.choice: high place (Literal, Balanced); hilltop shrine (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this word in these books.

decisions.choice: the detestable god (Balanced); the disgusting god (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

source.text: וְכֵ֣ן עָשָׂ֔ה לְכָל־נָשָׁ֖יו הַנָּכְרִיּ֑וֹת מַקְטִיר֥וֹת וּֽמְזַבְּח֖וֹת לֵאלֹהֵיהֶֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And thus he did for all his wives the foreign [ones], burning and sacrificing to their gods.

en.L: And so he did for all his foreign wives, who were burning [offerings] and sacrificing to their gods.
en.B: He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned offerings and sacrificed to their gods.
en.R: He did the same for all his foreign wives, so that they could burn offerings and make sacrifices to their own gods.

decisions.choice: burning and sacrificing: the wives did it
decisions.reason: The two verbs are feminine plural: it was the wives who offered to their gods. Solomon provided the shrines where they did it.

decisions.choice: burning: making offerings go up in smoke
decisions.reason: As at 3:3, the verb can mean burning incense or burning the parts of sacrifices on an altar; here it stands beside "sacrificing" as one act of worship.

decisions.choice: burning [offerings] (Literal); burned offerings (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb has no object in Hebrew; English needs one, as at 3:3.

source.text: וַיִּתְאַנַּ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בִּשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה כִּֽי־נָטָ֣ה לְבָב֗וֹ מֵעִ֤ם יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַנִּרְאָ֥ה אֵלָ֖יו פַּעֲמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And was angry Yahweh with Solomon, for had turned his heart from with Yahweh [the] God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} became angry with Solomon, for his heart had turned from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, who had twice appeared to him
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with Solomon, because Solomon had turned away from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, had appeared to Solomon two times.

decisions.choice: who had appeared to him twice: at Gibeon and after the temple
decisions.reason: Yahweh appeared to Solomon in a dream at Gibeon (3:5) and again when the temple was finished (9:2). In the second appearance he warned Solomon of what would follow if he served other gods (9:6-9).

decisions.choice: his heart had turned away: the reason for the anger
decisions.reason: Yahweh's anger is not a burst of temper but the response to a broken covenant. The same verb "turn" was used of the wives in verses 3-4.

decisions.choice: Solomon had turned away; had appeared to Solomon
decisions.reason: Readable names Solomon where the Hebrew says "his heart" and "him", and breaks the long sentence.

source.text: וְצִוָּ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ עַל־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לְבִ֨לְתִּי־לֶ֔כֶת אַחֲרֵ֖י אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וְלֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔ר אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֖ה יְהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: and he had commanded him concerning the matter this, not to go after gods other; but not he kept what commanded Yahweh.

en.L: and had commanded him concerning this matter, not to go after other gods; but he did not keep what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded.
en.B: and had commanded him about this very matter, that he must not follow other gods. But Solomon did not keep what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded.
en.R: He had told Solomon not to follow other gods. But Solomon did not obey what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded.

decisions.choice: commanded him concerning this matter: the warnings of 6:12 and 9:6
decisions.reason: Yahweh had told Solomon that the promise to David depended on keeping his commands (6:12), and had warned him plainly against serving other gods (9:6-7).

decisions.choice: he did not keep: Solomon is the subject
decisions.reason: The verb looks back to Solomon in verse 9; Yahweh is named again only as the one who commanded.

decisions.choice: Solomon
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Solomon so that "he" is not taken for the LORD.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה לִשְׁלֹמֹ֗ה יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָֽיְתָה־זֹּ֣את עִמָּ֔ךְ וְלֹ֤א שָׁמַ֨רְתָּ֙ בְּרִיתִ֣י וְחֻקֹּתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתִי עָלֶ֑יךָ קָרֹ֨עַ אֶקְרַ֤ע אֶת־הַמַּמְלָכָה֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ וּנְתַתִּ֖יהָ לְעַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Solomon, Because that has been this with you, and not you have kept my covenant and my statutes which I commanded to you, tearing I will tear the kingdom from on you, and I will give it to your servant.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Solomon, "Because this has been [so] with you, and you have not kept {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes that I commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Solomon, "Since this is what you have done, and you have not kept {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes that I commanded you, I will certainly tear the kingdom from you and give it to your servant.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Solomon, "You have done this. You have not kept {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, and you have not obeyed the laws I gave you. So I will surely tear the kingdom away from you and give it to one of your officials.

decisions.choice: this has been with you: this is how you have acted
decisions.reason: The phrase sums up what Solomon has done and what was in his mind; Yahweh names it as the cause of what follows.

decisions.choice: I will surely tear: a certain judgment
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. "Tear" pictures the kingdom ripped like a garment, as Samuel's robe was torn when Saul was rejected (1 Samuel 15:27-28), and it prepares for Ahijah's cloak (verse 30).

decisions.choice: your servant: one of Solomon's own officials
decisions.reason: The kingdom will not pass to Solomon's son but to a man who serves under him. Verse 26 shows who he is: Jeroboam, Solomon's official.

decisions.choice: one of your officials
decisions.reason: The word for servant here means a royal official, as in these books; Literal and Balanced keep "your servant".

decisions.choice: the laws I gave you
decisions.reason: Readable says "laws" for statutes, as elsewhere.

source.text: אַךְ־בְּיָמֶ֨יךָ֙ לֹ֣א אֶעֱשֶׂ֔נָּה לְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יךָ מִיַּ֥ד בִּנְךָ֖ אֶקְרָעֶֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: Only in your days not I will do it, for [the] sake of David your father; from [the] hand of your son I will tear it.

en.L: Only, in your days I will not do it, for the sake of David your father; from the hand of your son I will tear it.
en.B: Yet I will not do it in your lifetime, for the sake of your father David. I will tear it out of your son's hand.
en.R: But because of your father David, I will not do this while you are alive. I will tear it away from your son.

decisions.choice: for the sake of David: the promise to David's line
decisions.reason: Yahweh had promised David that his faithful love would not be taken from David's son as it was taken from Saul (2 Samuel 7:15). The judgment is delayed and limited because of that promise.

decisions.choice: from the hand of your son: out of his power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control. The kingdom will be torn from Solomon's son, Rehoboam (12:16-20).

source.text: רַ֤ק אֶת־כָּל־הַמַּמְלָכָה֙ לֹ֣א אֶקְרָ֔ע שֵׁ֥בֶט אֶחָ֖ד אֶתֵּ֣ן לִבְנֶ֑ךָ לְמַ֨עַן֙ דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֔י וּלְמַ֥עַן יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּחָֽרְתִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: Only all the kingdom not I will tear; tribe one I will give to your son, for [the] sake of David my servant, and for [the] sake of Jerusalem which I have chosen.

en.L: Only, I will not tear away all the kingdom; one tribe I will give to your son, for the sake of David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave, and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen."
en.B: But I will not tear away the whole kingdom. I will give your son one tribe because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David and because of Jerusalem, which I have chosen."
en.R: But I will not take the whole kingdom away. I will give your son one tribe. I will do this because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David, and because of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen."

decisions.choice: one tribe: Judah
decisions.reason: The tribe left to David's line is Judah, with the city of Jerusalem (12:20). See verse 32 for how the count of tribes works.

decisions.choice: my servant David: a title of honor
decisions.reason: Yahweh calls David "my servant" as one who belonged to him and served him faithfully (2 Samuel 7:5, 8). The word is the one used for a slave, which shows how fully David was Yahweh's.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem which I have chosen: the place of Yahweh's name
decisions.reason: Yahweh chose Jerusalem as the place for his name and his temple (8:16, 44; Deuteronomy 12:5). Keeping a tribe for David keeps that city in the hands of David's line.

decisions.choice: my slave (Literal); my servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for "my servant David" in these books.

source.text: וַיָּ֨קֶם יְהוָ֤ה שָׂטָן֙ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֵ֖ת הֲדַ֣ד הָאֲדֹמִ֑י מִזֶּ֧רַע הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ ה֖וּא בֶּאֱדֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And raised up Yahweh an adversary to Solomon, Hadad the Edomite; of [the] seed of the king he [was] in Edom.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} raised up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite; he [was] of the royal line in Edom.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} raised up an adversary against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite, who was of the royal family of Edom.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} caused an enemy to rise up against Solomon. This was Hadad from Edom, who belonged to Edom's royal family.

decisions.choice: an adversary: a human opponent, not the name Satan
decisions.reason: The word is a common noun here, without the article: an opponent who stands against someone, as in 1 Samuel 29:4 and 2 Samuel 19:23. The same word later names the heavenly accuser (Job 1:6; Zechariah 3:1), but in this chapter it is used of Hadad and Rezon, men raised up as Solomon's enemies.

decisions.choice: an adversary against Solomon: the end of the rest he had boasted of
decisions.reason: Solomon had told Hiram that Yahweh had given him rest on every side, with "no adversary" (5:18). Now Yahweh himself raises adversaries against him.

decisions.choice: the LORD raised up: Yahweh uses human enemies to discipline his people
decisions.reason: As in Judges, Yahweh is said to raise up the enemies who trouble Israel when it turns from him (Judges 2:14; 3:12). The verb is the one used for raising up judges and kings.

decisions.choice: enemy
decisions.reason: Readable says "enemy" for "adversary", a less common English word.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּֽהְי֤וֹת דָּוִד֙ אֶת־אֱד֔וֹם בַּעֲל֗וֹת יוֹאָב֙ שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֔א לְקַבֵּ֖ר אֶת־הַחֲלָלִ֑ים וַיַּ֥ךְ כָּל־זָכָ֖ר בֶּאֱדֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when was David with Edom, when went up Joab [the] commander of the army to bury the slain, and he struck down every male in Edom;

en.L: And it happened, when David was with Edom, when Joab the commander of the army went up to bury the slain, that he struck down every male in Edom;
en.B: Earlier, when David was at war with Edom, Joab the commander of the army went up to bury the dead and struck down every male in Edom;
en.R: Years before, David had been at war with Edom. Joab, the army commander, went there to bury the Israelites who had been killed, and he killed every male in Edom.

decisions.choice: when David was with Edom: David's war against Edom
decisions.reason: David defeated Edom and put garrisons there, and all Edom became his servants (2 Samuel 8:13-14; Psalm 60:2). This verse tells part of that war that 2 Samuel does not.

decisions.choice: with Edom: engaged with Edom in war
decisions.reason: The small word "with" here means dealing with an enemy in battle. Some ancient translations read "when David struck Edom", which gives the same sense.

decisions.choice: the slain: Israel's dead from the war
decisions.reason: Joab went up to bury the Israelite soldiers who had fallen. While there he carried out a slaughter of Edom's men.

decisions.choice: every male: the men of Edom who could be found
decisions.reason: The phrase is sweeping, but Hadad and his men escaped (verse 17) and Edom remained a people. It means a slaughter of the males in the land, not the death of every one.

decisions.choice: Earlier
decisions.reason: The story goes back to David's reign; Balanced marks the flashback with one word.

decisions.choice: Years before; the Israelites who had been killed
decisions.reason: Readable marks the flashback and says whose dead were buried (m3).

source.text: כִּ֣י שֵׁ֧שֶׁת חֳדָשִׁ֛ים יָֽשַׁב־שָׁ֥ם יוֹאָ֖ב וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עַד־הִכְרִ֥ית כָּל־זָכָ֖ר בֶּאֱדֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: For six months remained there Joab and all Israel, until he had cut off every male in Edom.

en.L: For six months Joab and all Israel remained there, until he had cut off every male in Edom.
en.B: For Joab and all Israel stayed there six months, until he had destroyed every male in Edom.
en.R: Joab and the whole Israelite army stayed there for six months, until they had killed every male in Edom.

decisions.choice: for: the verse explains the slaughter
decisions.reason: The verse tells how the killing in verse 15 was done: Joab stayed in the land until the work was finished.

decisions.choice: all Israel: the army of Israel
decisions.reason: "All Israel" here means the fighting men who went with Joab, as often in these books (2 Samuel 11:1).

decisions.choice: the whole Israelite army; they had killed
decisions.reason: Readable says who "all Israel" was (m2) and makes the army the subject of the killing.

source.text: וַיִּבְרַ֣ח אֲדַ֡ד הוּא֩ וַאֲנָשִׁ֨ים אֲדֹמִיִּ֜ים מֵעַבְדֵ֥י אָבִ֛יו אִתּ֖וֹ לָב֣וֹא מִצְרָ֑יִם וַהֲדַ֖ד נַ֥עַר קָטָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And fled Adad, he and men Edomite from [the] servants of his father with him, to go [to] Egypt; and Hadad [was] a boy small.

en.L: And Hadad fled, he and some Edomite men of his father's servants with him, to go to Egypt; and Hadad [was] a small boy.
en.B: But Hadad escaped to Egypt with some Edomite officials who had served his father. Hadad was only a young boy at the time.
en.R: But Hadad escaped to Egypt with some Edomite officials who had served his father. Hadad was just a young boy then.

decisions.choice: Hadad: here spelled Adad
decisions.reason: In this verse the Hebrew writes the name without its first letter, Adad, a known form of the same name. It is the same man; the spelling is kept as one name in translation.

decisions.choice: his father's servants: officials of the Edomite king
decisions.reason: The servants of a king's household were his officials and attendants. They saved the young prince from Joab's slaughter.

decisions.choice: a small boy: still a child
decisions.reason: The words mean a young child, too young to rule; he grew up in Egypt (verses 19-20).

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in these books, Balanced and Readable say "officials" for a king's servants.

source.text: וַיָּקֻ֨מוּ֙ מִמִּדְיָ֔ן וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ פָּארָ֑ן וַיִּקְחוּ֩ אֲנָשִׁ֨ים עִמָּ֜ם מִפָּארָ֗ן וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּתֶּן־ל֣וֹ בַ֗יִת וְלֶ֨חֶם֙ אָ֣מַר ל֔וֹ וְאֶ֖רֶץ נָ֥תַן לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they arose from Midian and came [to] Paran, and took men with them from Paran, and came [to] Egypt to Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he gave to him a house, and food he assigned to him, and land he gave to him.

en.L: And they set out from Midian and came to Paran, and they took men with them from Paran and came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he gave him a house, and assigned him food, and gave him land.
en.B: They set out from Midian and came to Paran. Taking men with them from Paran, they came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt. Pharaoh provided Hadad with a house and food, and gave him land.
en.R: They left Midian and went to Paran. There more men joined them, and they went on to Egypt, to Pharaoh the king. Pharaoh gave Hadad a house, food, and some land.

decisions.choice: Midian and Paran: the desert route to Egypt
decisions.reason: Midian lay southeast of Edom, and the wilderness of Paran lay in the Sinai, between Edom and Egypt (Numbers 10:12). The fugitives passed through desert country on their way.

decisions.choice: food he assigned to him: Pharaoh set his provisions
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "say"; here it means to give an order for something, so that Hadad was fed from the king's stores.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh received him: a rival prince kept at court
decisions.reason: Kings sometimes sheltered the exiled princes of neighboring lands, who might later be useful against their enemies. Jeroboam too will find refuge in Egypt (verse 40).

decisions.choice: Hadad
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Hadad where the Hebrew says "him", since "they" have just been the subject.

source.text: וַיִּמְצָא֙ הֲדַ֥ד חֵ֛ן בְּעֵינֵ֥י פַרְעֹ֖ה מְאֹ֑ד וַיִּתֶּן־ל֤וֹ אִשָּׁה֙ אֶת־אֲח֣וֹת אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ אֲח֖וֹת תַּחְפְּנֵ֥יס הַגְּבִירָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And found Hadad favor in [the] eyes of Pharaoh greatly, and he gave to him a wife, [the] sister of his wife, [the] sister of Tahpenes the queen.

en.L: And Hadad found great favor in the eyes of Pharaoh, and he gave him a wife, the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
en.B: Hadad won so much favor with Pharaoh that Pharaoh gave him his own wife's sister in marriage, the sister of Queen Tahpenes.
en.R: Pharaoh liked Hadad very much, so he gave him a wife. She was the sister of Pharaoh's own wife, Queen Tahpenes.

decisions.choice: found favor in the eyes of: was looked on with kindness
decisions.reason: To find favor in someone's eyes is to win their good will (Genesis 39:4; 1 Samuel 16:22).

decisions.choice: the queen: the great lady of the court
decisions.reason: The word means a lady of high rank. Here it is Pharaoh's chief wife; in Judah it names the queen mother (15:13).

decisions.choice: a wife from Pharaoh's house: a match for Solomon's own marriage
decisions.reason: As Solomon married a daughter of Pharaoh (3:1), so his enemy is joined to Pharaoh's family. Egypt is friend to both sides.

source.text: וַתֵּ֨לֶד ל֜וֹ אֲח֣וֹת תַּחְפְּנֵ֗יס אֵ֚ת גְּנֻבַ֣ת בְּנ֔וֹ וַתִּגְמְלֵ֣הוּ תַחְפְּנֵ֔ס בְּת֖וֹךְ בֵּ֣ית פַּרְעֹ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י גְנֻבַת֙ בֵּ֣ית פַּרְעֹ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י פַרְעֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And bore to him [the] sister of Tahpenes Genubath his son, and weaned him Tahpenes in [the] midst of [the] house of Pharaoh; and was Genubath [in the] house of Pharaoh among [the] sons of Pharaoh.

en.L: And the sister of Tahpenes bore him Genubath his son, and Tahpenes weaned him in the midst of Pharaoh's house; and Genubath was [in] Pharaoh's house among the sons of Pharaoh.
en.B: Tahpenes' sister bore him a son, Genubath, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh's palace. Genubath lived in Pharaoh's household among Pharaoh's own sons.
en.R: Tahpenes' sister had a son named Genubath. Tahpenes brought him up in the palace, and Genubath grew up there with Pharaoh's sons.

decisions.choice: weaned: brought up the child, with a weaning feast
decisions.reason: A child was weaned at two or three years old, and the day could be marked with a feast (Genesis 21:8). That the queen weaned the boy shows she treated him as one of the royal children.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh's house: the palace and the royal household
decisions.reason: The house of a king is both his palace and his family. Genubath was raised as a member of Pharaoh's family.

decisions.choice: brought him up
decisions.reason: Readable says what the weaning meant here (m1) rather than the act itself.

source.text: וַהֲדַ֞ד שָׁמַ֣ע בְּמִצְרַ֗יִם כִּֽי־שָׁכַ֤ב דָּוִד֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וְכִי־מֵ֖ת יוֹאָ֣ב שַֽׂר־הַצָּבָ֑א וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הֲדַד֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה שַׁלְּחֵ֖נִי וְאֵלֵ֥ךְ אֶל־אַרְצִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And Hadad heard in Egypt that had lain down David with his fathers, and that had died Joab [the] commander of the army; and said Hadad to Pharaoh, Send me away, and I will go to my land.

en.L: And Hadad heard in Egypt that David had lain down with his fathers and that Joab the commander of the army was dead, and Hadad said to Pharaoh, "Send me away, so that I may go to my land."
en.B: While in Egypt, Hadad heard that David had rested with his ancestors and that Joab the commander of the army was dead. So Hadad said to Pharaoh, "Let me go, so that I may return to my own country."
en.R: In Egypt Hadad heard that David had died, and that Joab the army commander was dead too. So Hadad said to Pharaoh, "Let me go back to my own country."

decisions.choice: lain down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The formula Kings uses for the death of a king, as at 2:10.

decisions.choice: Joab was dead: Edom's destroyer was gone
decisions.reason: Joab was put to death at the start of Solomon's reign (2:34). With David and Joab both dead, Hadad saw his chance to return.

decisions.choice: lain down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula is worded the same way at each level throughout Kings.

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ פַרְעֹ֗ה כִּ֠י מָה־אַתָּ֤ה חָסֵר֙ עִמִּ֔י וְהִנְּךָ֥ מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ לָלֶ֣כֶת אֶל־אַרְצֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀לֹ֔א כִּ֥י שַׁלֵּ֖חַ תְּשַׁלְּחֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Pharaoh, But what you [are] lacking with me, that behold you [are] seeking to go to your land? And he said, No, but surely you shall send me away.

en.L: And Pharaoh said to him, "But what are you lacking with me, that now you are seeking to go to your land?" And he said, "Nothing; but you must surely send me away."
en.B: Pharaoh said to him, "What do you lack here with me, that you now want to go back to your own country?" "Nothing," Hadad answered, "but please let me go!"
en.R: Pharaoh asked him, "Have I not given you everything you need? Why do you want to go back to your own country?" Hadad answered, "I have everything I need. But please let me go."

decisions.choice: you must surely send me away: an urgent request
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. Hadad presses his request even though he has nothing to complain of.

decisions.choice: No: nothing is lacking
decisions.reason: Hadad's "no" answers Pharaoh's question: he lacks nothing in Egypt. The account does not say whether Pharaoh let him go, but verse 25 shows he went home and troubled Israel.

decisions.choice: Have I not given you everything you need? Why ...
decisions.reason: Readable splits Pharaoh's question into two shorter questions and turns Hadad's "No" into a full sentence.

source.text: וַיָּ֨קֶם אֱלֹהִ֥ים לוֹ֙ שָׂטָ֔ן אֶת־רְז֖וֹן בֶּן־אֶלְיָדָ֑ע אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּרַ֗ח מֵאֵ֛ת הֲדַדְעֶ֥זֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־צוֹבָ֖ה אֲדֹנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And raised up God to him an adversary, Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from Hadadezer king of Zobah his master.

en.L: And God raised up an adversary against him, Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from Hadadezer king of Zobah, his master.
en.B: God also raised up another adversary against Solomon, Rezon son of Eliada, who had run away from his master, Hadadezer king of Zobah.
en.R: God also caused another enemy to rise up against Solomon. This was Rezon son of Eliada. Rezon had run away from his master, Hadadezer, the king of Zobah.

decisions.choice: an adversary: an opponent, as in verse 14
decisions.reason: The same common noun as in verse 14: a human enemy, not the heavenly accuser.

decisions.choice: Hadadezer king of Zobah: the Aramean king David defeated
decisions.reason: Zobah was an Aramean kingdom north of Damascus. David defeated Hadadezer and his allies (2 Samuel 8:3-8; 10:6-19). Rezon was one of his officers who broke away.

decisions.choice: God: the same God as in verse 14
decisions.reason: This verse says "God" where verse 14 says "Yahweh"; it is the same God at work, raising a second adversary.

decisions.choice: another; Solomon
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Solomon for "him" and add "another" (Readable "also ... another"), since this is the second adversary.

source.text: וַיִּקְבֹּ֤ץ עָלָיו֙ אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַיְהִ֣י שַׂר־גְּד֔וּד בַּהֲרֹ֥ג דָּוִ֖ד אֹתָ֑ם וַיֵּלְכ֤וּ דַמֶּ֨שֶׂק֙ וַיֵּ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֔הּ וַֽיִּמְלְכ֖וּ בְּדַמָּֽשֶׂק׃

records.literal_gloss: And he gathered to him men, and he became commander of a raiding band, when killed David them; and they went [to] Damascus and dwelt in it, and reigned in Damascus.

en.L: And he gathered men to himself and became commander of a raiding band, when David killed them; and they went to Damascus and settled in it, and reigned in Damascus.
en.B: He gathered men around him and became commander of a band of raiders after David slaughtered the forces of Zobah. They went to Damascus, settled there, and ruled in Damascus.
en.R: After David defeated the armies of Zobah, Rezon gathered a group of men around him and became the commander of a band of raiders. They went to Damascus, settled there, and took control of the city.

decisions.choice: when David killed them: the men of Zobah
decisions.reason: "Them" refers back to Hadadezer's people in verse 23. David's slaughter of Zobah's army (2 Samuel 8:3-5; 10:18) left Rezon free to gather men of his own.

decisions.choice: a raiding band: an armed troop living by raids
decisions.reason: The word names a band of armed men who make raids, as David's own men once did (1 Samuel 30:8, 15).

decisions.choice: they reigned: Rezon and his men took power
decisions.reason: The verb is plural: Rezon's band took control of Damascus, with Rezon as its king (verse 25). Some ancient translations read "they made him king" or "he reigned".

decisions.choice: the forces of Zobah (Balanced); the armies of Zobah (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "them" are (m1); Readable puts the time clause first.

decisions.choice: took control of the city
decisions.reason: Readable says what "reigned in Damascus" meant for a band that had just arrived.

source.text: וַיְהִ֨י שָׂטָ֤ן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כָּל־יְמֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וְאֶת־הָרָעָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֲדָ֑ד וַיָּ֨קָץ֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ עַל־אֲרָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he was an adversary to Israel all [the] days of Solomon, and with the harm which Hadad [did]; and he loathed Israel and reigned over Aram.

en.L: And he was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, along with the harm that Hadad [did]; and he loathed Israel and reigned over Aram.
en.B: Rezon was Israel's adversary as long as Solomon lived, adding to the harm that Hadad did. He loathed Israel and reigned over Aram.
en.R: Rezon was Israel's enemy as long as Solomon lived. He made trouble for Israel, just as Hadad did. Rezon hated Israel, and he ruled as king over Aram.

decisions.choice: along with the harm that Hadad did; he reigned over Aram
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very brief: the verb for what Hadad did is not written, and the last clause may be about Rezon or Hadad. The ancient Greek translation reads "Edom" for "Aram" and makes the last words a summary of Hadad's reign. The Hebrew, followed here, ends with Rezon as king of Aram.

decisions.choice: loathed: felt disgust and hostility toward
decisions.reason: The verb means to feel loathing or dread (Numbers 21:5; 22:3). Rezon's hatred of Israel lasted all through Solomon's reign.

decisions.choice: Aram: the Aramean kingdom of Damascus
decisions.reason: Aram is the land of the Arameans, roughly modern Syria. With Damascus as its capital it became one of Israel's chief enemies (15:18; 20:1).

decisions.choice: Rezon
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Rezon, since Hadad has just been mentioned.

decisions.choice: enemy; hated
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer words "enemy" for adversary and "hated" for loathed.

source.text: וְיָרָבְעָם֩ בֶּן־נְבָ֨ט אֶפְרָתִ֜י מִן־הַצְּרֵדָ֗ה וְשֵׁ֤ם אִמּוֹ֙ צְרוּעָה֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה אַלְמָנָ֔ה עֶ֖בֶד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַיָּ֥רֶם יָ֖ד בַּמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephrathite from the Zeredah, and [the] name of his mother Zeruah, a woman widow, [was] a servant of Solomon; and he raised a hand against the king.

en.L: And Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephrathite from Zeredah, whose mother's name [was] Zeruah, a widow, [was] a servant of Solomon; and he lifted up a hand against the king.
en.B: Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah, was one of Solomon's officials. His mother's name was Zeruah, a widow. He rebelled against the king.
en.R: Jeroboam son of Nebat was one of Solomon's officials. He came from the town of Zeredah in Ephraim. His mother was a widow named Zeruah. Jeroboam rebelled against the king.

decisions.choice: an Ephrathite: a man of the tribe of Ephraim
decisions.reason: The word can mean a man of Ephrathah, the clan of Bethlehem (Ruth 1:2), but here, as in Judges 12:5 and 1 Samuel 1:1, it means an Ephraimite. Zeredah was in the hill country of Ephraim.

decisions.choice: lifted up a hand against the king: rebelled
decisions.reason: To raise the hand against someone is to rise up against him. Verses 27-40 tell how Jeroboam's rebellion came about.

decisions.choice: a widow: his father was dead
decisions.reason: Naming the mother, and that she was a widow, may stress Jeroboam's humble start: the man who will take ten tribes rose from a fatherless home.

decisions.choice: an Ephraimite (Balanced); in Ephraim (Readable); one of Solomon's officials
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "Ephrathite" means here (m1), and say "officials" for a king's servants, as elsewhere.

source.text: וְזֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁר־הֵרִ֥ים יָ֖ד בַּמֶּ֑לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ בָּנָ֣ה אֶת־הַמִּלּ֔וֹא סָגַ֕ר אֶת־פֶּ֕רֶץ עִ֖יר דָּוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And this [is] the matter [for] which he raised a hand against the king: Solomon built the Millo; he closed up the breach of [the] city of David his father.

en.L: And this [is] the account of how he lifted up a hand against the king: Solomon built the Millo; he closed up the breach of the City of David his father.
en.B: This is how he came to rebel against the king. Solomon had built the Millo and closed up the gap in the wall of the City of David his father.
en.R: This is the story of how he rebelled. Solomon was building the Millo and repairing a broken part of the wall of the City of David, his father's city.

decisions.choice: the matter: the account, the circumstances
decisions.reason: The word means a word or a matter. Here it introduces the story of how the rebellion began, as at 9:15.

decisions.choice: the Millo: a terraced structure in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The name means "filling". It was probably a filled-in platform or terrace on the slope of the City of David that supported buildings above it (9:15, 24; 2 Samuel 5:9). Its exact nature is not certain.

decisions.choice: the breach: a gap in the city wall
decisions.reason: Solomon closed up a gap left in the walls of the old city. The work set the scene for Jeroboam's rise (verse 28).

decisions.choice: in the wall
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the gap was.

source.text: וְהָאִ֥ישׁ יָרָבְעָ֖ם גִּבּ֣וֹר חָ֑יִל וַיַּ֨רְא שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה אֶת־הַנַּ֗עַר כִּֽי־עֹשֵׂ֤ה מְלָאכָה֙ ה֔וּא וַיַּפְקֵ֣ד אֹת֔וֹ לְכָל־סֵ֖בֶל בֵּ֥ית יוֹסֵֽף׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the man Jeroboam [was] a mighty man of strength; and saw Solomon the young man, that doing work he [was], and he appointed him over all [the] forced labor of [the] house of Joseph.

en.L: And the man Jeroboam [was] a mighty man of ability; and Solomon saw the young man, that he was doing the work, and he appointed him over all the forced labor of the house of Joseph.
en.B: Jeroboam was a strong and capable man. When Solomon saw how well the young man did his work, he put him in charge of all the forced labor of the house of Joseph.
en.R: Jeroboam was a very able man. Solomon saw what a good worker the young man was, so he put him in charge of all the work crews from the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh.

decisions.choice: a mighty man of ability: strong, capable and respected
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean a warrior, a man of wealth and standing (Ruth 2:1; 1 Samuel 9:1), or a capable man. Here it is Jeroboam's ability and energy that Solomon notices.

decisions.choice: forced labor: work the king required of his people
decisions.reason: The word means burden-bearing. Solomon drafted Israelites to work in turns on his building projects (5:27-28; 12:4). The burden would become the people's complaint against his son.

decisions.choice: the house of Joseph: the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh
decisions.reason: Joseph's two sons became the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, the strongest of the northern tribes. Jeroboam was put over the labor drafted from his own people.

decisions.choice: the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh
decisions.reason: Readable names the tribes meant by "the house of Joseph" (m3).

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא וְיָֽרָבְעָ֖ם יָצָ֣א מִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיִּמְצָ֣א אֹת֡וֹ אֲחִיָּה֩ הַשִּׁילֹנִ֨י הַנָּבִ֜יא בַּדֶּ֗רֶךְ וְה֤וּא מִתְכַּסֶּה֙ בְּשַׂלְמָ֣ה חֲדָשָׁ֔ה וּשְׁנֵיהֶ֥ם לְבַדָּ֖ם בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was at the time that, and Jeroboam went out from Jerusalem, and found him Ahijah the Shilonite, the prophet, on the road; and he [was] covering himself with a cloak new, and [the] two of them [were] by themselves in the field.

en.L: And it happened at that time, when Jeroboam went out from Jerusalem, that Ahijah the Shilonite, the prophet, found him on the road; and he was wearing a new cloak, and the two of them [were] alone in the field.
en.B: At that time, as Jeroboam was going out of Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met him on the road. Ahijah had on a new cloak, and the two were alone out in the country.
en.R: One day Jeroboam was leaving Jerusalem. On the road the prophet Ahijah, from the town of Shiloh, met him. Ahijah was wearing a new coat, and the two of them were alone out in the country.

decisions.choice: he was wearing a new cloak: Ahijah
decisions.reason: "He" is most naturally Ahijah, the last person named; verse 30 speaks of the cloak "that was on him", and the prophet uses his own cloak for the sign.

decisions.choice: the Shilonite: from Shiloh
decisions.reason: Shiloh in Ephraim was where the tabernacle and the ark once stood (Joshua 18:1; 1 Samuel 1:3). A prophet from that old northern sanctuary now announces the northern kingdom.

decisions.choice: a cloak: the outer garment
decisions.reason: The word names the large outer garment worn over the tunic. Being new, it was whole and strong, which makes the tearing more striking.

decisions.choice: Ahijah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Ahijah as the one wearing the cloak (m1).

source.text: וַיִּתְפֹּ֣שׂ אֲחִיָּ֔ה בַּשַּׂלְמָ֥ה הַחֲדָשָׁ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֑יו וַיִּ֨קְרָעֶ֔הָ שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר קְרָעִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And seized Ahijah the cloak the new which [was] on him, and tore it [into] twelve pieces.

en.L: And Ahijah took hold of the new cloak that [was] on him, and tore it [into] twelve pieces.
en.B: Ahijah took hold of the new cloak he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces.
en.R: Ahijah took hold of his new coat and tore it into twelve pieces.

decisions.choice: tore it: an acted prophecy
decisions.reason: Prophets sometimes acted out their message (1 Samuel 15:27-28; Jeremiah 19:10-11). The torn cloak shows what Yahweh said in verse 11: the kingdom will be torn apart.

decisions.choice: twelve pieces: the twelve tribes of Israel
decisions.reason: The pieces stand for the twelve tribes, as verse 31 explains.

decisions.choice: that was on him: Ahijah's own cloak
decisions.reason: As in verse 29, "him" is taken as Ahijah. The words could refer to Jeroboam, but the prophet acting with his own garment fits the sign best.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לְיָֽרָבְעָ֔ם קַח־לְךָ֖ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה קְרָעִ֑ים כִּ֣י כֹה֩ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הִנְנִ֨י קֹרֵ֤עַ אֶת־הַמַּמְלָכָה֙ מִיַּ֣ד שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וְנָתַתִּ֣י לְךָ֔ אֵ֖ת עֲשָׂרָ֥ה הַשְּׁבָטִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to Jeroboam, Take for yourself ten pieces, for thus says Yahweh [the] God of Israel, Behold I [am] tearing the kingdom from [the] hand of Solomon, and I will give to you the ten tribes,

en.L: And he said to Jeroboam, "Take for yourself ten pieces, for thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: 'Look, I am tearing the kingdom from the hand of Solomon, and I will give you the ten tribes,
en.B: Then he said to Jeroboam, "Take ten pieces for yourself, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: 'I am about to tear the kingdom out of Solomon's hand and give you ten tribes,
en.R: Then he said to Jeroboam, "Take ten of these pieces for yourself. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: 'I am going to tear the kingdom away from Solomon. I will give ten of the tribes to you.

decisions.choice: I am tearing: an act about to happen
decisions.reason: The participle after "look" announces what Yahweh is about to do. The tearing would happen under Solomon's son (verses 12, 35).

decisions.choice: the ten tribes: the tribes outside Judah
decisions.reason: The ten pieces stand for the ten tribes that will follow Jeroboam (12:20). See verse 32 on the remaining tribe.

decisions.choice: from the hand of: out of the power of
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, the hand stands for power and rule.

decisions.choice: thus says / says this / This is what ... says
decisions.reason: The wording kept for the messenger formula at each level in these books.

decisions.choice: Look
decisions.reason: Literal says "look" for the Hebrew word that calls attention, instead of the older "behold"; Balanced and Readable carry it in "about to" and "going to".

source.text: וְהַשֵּׁ֥בֶט הָאֶחָ֖ד יִֽהְיֶה־לּ֑וֹ לְמַ֣עַן׀עַבְדִּ֣י דָוִ֗ד וּלְמַ֨עַן֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֣רְתִּי בָ֔הּ מִכֹּ֖ל שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: and the tribe the one shall be to him for [the] sake of my servant David and for [the] sake of Jerusalem the city which I have chosen in it from all [the] tribes of Israel,

en.L: and the one tribe shall be his, for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel,
en.B: but one tribe will remain his because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David and because of Jerusalem, the city I chose from among all the tribes of Israel,
en.R: But Solomon's family will keep one tribe. I will do this because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David, and because of Jerusalem. Out of all the tribes of Israel, I chose this city as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own.

decisions.choice: the one tribe: Judah, with Benjamin joined to it
decisions.reason: Twelve pieces, ten given to Jeroboam and one kept, leave one unaccounted for. The one tribe is Judah; Benjamin, whose land held part of Jerusalem, stayed with it (12:21), and Simeon's towns lay within Judah (Joshua 19:1, 9). The count may treat Judah and Benjamin as one, or leave the twelfth piece unexplained.

decisions.choice: the city I have chosen out of all the tribes: Jerusalem as Yahweh's one place
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy speaks of the place Yahweh would choose out of all the tribes for his name (Deuteronomy 12:5). Yahweh keeps Jerusalem for David's line because he chose it.

decisions.choice: my slave (Literal); my servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

decisions.choice: Solomon's family
decisions.reason: Readable says who "him" is: the tribe stays with Solomon's line, as verse 36 says.

source.text: יַ֣עַן׀אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲזָב֗וּנִי וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲווּ֮ לְעַשְׁתֹּרֶת֮ אֱלֹהֵ֣י צִֽדֹנִין֒ לִכְמוֹשׁ֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב וּלְמִלְכֹּ֖ם אֱלֹהֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־עַמּ֑וֹן וְלֹֽא־הָלְכ֣וּ בִדְרָכַ֗י לַעֲשׂ֨וֹת הַיָּשָׁ֧ר בְּעֵינַ֛י וְחֻקֹּתַ֥י וּמִשְׁפָּטַ֖י כְּדָוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: because that they have forsaken me, and have bowed down to Ashtoreth [the] god of [the] Sidonians, to Chemosh [the] god of Moab, and to Milcom [the] god of [the] sons of Ammon, and not they have walked in my ways to do the right in my eyes, and my statutes and my judgments, as David his father.

en.L: because they have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and bowed down to Ashtoreth the god of the Sidonians, to Chemosh the god of Moab, and to Milcom the god of the sons of Ammon, and have not walked in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ways, to do what [is] right in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes and [to keep] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments, as David his father [did].
en.B: because they have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and worshiped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites. They have not followed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ways, doing what is right in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight and keeping {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings, as his father David did.
en.R: I will do this because they have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They have worshiped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites. They have not lived the way I want them to live. They have not done what I say is right or obeyed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and rules, as Solomon's father David did.

decisions.choice: they have forsaken: Solomon and those who worshiped with him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verbs are plural. The ancient Greek, Syriac and Latin translations read "he has forsaken", which matches "as David his father" at the end. The Hebrew, followed here, includes the people who joined Solomon's worship of other gods.

decisions.choice: bowed down to: worshiped
decisions.reason: To bow down to a god is to worship it.

decisions.choice: the god of the Sidonians: Ashtoreth, a goddess
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the one word for "god" serves for a goddess. Here the three gods are given the plain title "god", not the scornful one of verses 5 and 7.

decisions.choice: goddess
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

decisions.choice: statutes, judgments / statutes, rulings / laws, rules
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these words in these books. Readable says "what I say is right" for "what is right in my eyes".

source.text: וְלֹֽא־אֶקַּ֥ח אֶת־כָּל־הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה מִיָּד֑וֹ כִּ֣י׀נָשִׂ֣יא אֲשִׁתֶ֗נּוּ כֹּ֚ל יְמֵ֣י חַיָּ֔יו לְמַ֨עַן דָּוִ֤ד עַבְדִּי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֣רְתִּי אֹת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖ר מִצְוֺתַ֥י וְחֻקֹּתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And not I will take all the kingdom from his hand, for ruler I will make him all [the] days of his life, for [the] sake of David my servant whom I chose him, who kept my commandments and my statutes.

en.L: But I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand, for I will make him leader all the days of his life, for the sake of David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave, whom I chose, who kept {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes.
en.B: Still, I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand. I will keep him as leader all the days of his life, for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David, whom I chose and who kept {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes.
en.R: But I will not take the whole kingdom away from Solomon. I will let him remain leader as long as he lives. I will do this because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David. I chose David, and he obeyed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands and laws.

decisions.choice: leader: one raised up to lead the people
decisions.reason: The word usually names a tribal leader. Used of a king, it stresses that he rules under Yahweh, by Yahweh's appointment (Ezekiel 34:24).

decisions.choice: who kept my commandments: David's loyalty
decisions.reason: David's sins are not hidden in Samuel, but he never turned to other gods and he repented when rebuked (2 Samuel 12:13). That loyalty is what Yahweh honors here.

decisions.choice: my slave (Literal); my servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

decisions.choice: leader
decisions.reason: The word is "leader" at every level in these books, as in the tribal lists; "ruler" is kept for *nagid* (14:7; 16:2).

source.text: וְלָקַחְתִּ֥י הַמְּלוּכָ֖ה מִיַּ֣ד בְּנ֑וֹ וּנְתַתִּ֣יהָ לְּךָ֔ אֵ֖ת עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת הַשְּׁבָטִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will take the kingship from [the] hand of his son and give it to you, the ten tribes.

en.L: And I will take the kingship from the hand of his son and give it to you, the ten tribes.
en.B: But I will take the kingdom from his son's hand and give you ten tribes of it.
en.R: But I will take the kingdom away from his son, and I will give you ten tribes.

decisions.choice: give it to you, the ten tribes: the part given is ten tribes
decisions.reason: "The ten tribes" stands beside "it" to say what part of the kingdom Jeroboam will receive.

decisions.choice: the kingship: royal rule
decisions.reason: The word means the rule itself, the right to reign. It is taken from Solomon's son, not from Solomon (verse 12).

source.text: וְלִבְנ֖וֹ אֶתֵּ֣ן שֵֽׁבֶט־אֶחָ֑ד לְמַ֣עַן הֱיֽוֹת־נִ֣יר לְדָֽוִיד־עַ֠בְדִּי כָּֽל־הַיָּמִ֤ים׀לְפָנַי֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֣רְתִּי לִ֔י לָשׂ֥וּם שְׁמִ֖י שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And to his son I will give tribe one, so that may be a lamp for David my servant all the days before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen for myself to put my name there.

en.L: And to his son I will give one tribe, so that there may be a lamp for David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave all the days before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} to put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name there.
en.B: To his son I will give one tribe, so that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David may always have a lamp before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in Jerusalem, the city I have chosen for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} to put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name there.
en.R: I will give one tribe to his son. Then {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David will always have a descendant ruling in Jerusalem before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, like a lamp that keeps burning. Jerusalem is the city I chose as the place where {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name would be honored.

decisions.choice: a lamp for David: a line of David's descendants that does not die out
decisions.reason: A lamp left burning in a house is a sign that the family lives on. A lamp for David in Jerusalem is a son of David on the throne there (15:4; 2 Kings 8:19; Psalm 132:17). Some take the word as a related noun meaning "dominion", but the picture of the lamp fits these passages.

decisions.choice: to put my name there: the place of Yahweh's presence and worship
decisions.reason: Yahweh's name stands for himself as he makes himself known. The place where he puts his name is the place where he is worshiped and hears prayer (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11; 1 Kings 8:29; 9:3).

decisions.choice: my slave (Literal); my servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

decisions.choice: a descendant ruling ... like a lamp that keeps burning
decisions.reason: Readable says what the lamp stands for (m1) and keeps the picture as a comparison.

decisions.choice: the place where my name would be honored
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of putting the name in a place (m2).

source.text: וְאֹתְךָ֣ אֶקַּ֔ח וּמָ֣לַכְתָּ֔ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־תְּאַוֶּ֖ה נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וְהָיִ֥יתָ מֶּ֖לֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And you I will take, and you shall reign over all that desires your soul, and you shall be king over Israel.

en.L: And you I will take, and you shall reign over all that your soul desires, and you shall be king over Israel.
en.B: As for you, I will take you, and you will reign over all that you desire; you will be king over Israel.
en.R: As for you, I will choose you. You will rule over all that you want to rule, and you will be king over Israel.

decisions.choice: all that your soul desires: everything you long for
decisions.reason: The soul here is the seat of desire. Abner made the same promise to David (2 Samuel 3:21). It may hint that Jeroboam already wanted the throne.

decisions.choice: Israel: here the northern tribes
decisions.reason: From now on "Israel" often names the ten northern tribes, the kingdom Jeroboam will rule, as against Judah (12:19-20).

decisions.choice: choose
decisions.reason: Readable says "choose" for "take", the sense of the verb here.

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־תִּשְׁמַע֮ אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲצַוֶּךָ֒ וְהָלַכְתָּ֣ בִדְרָכַ֗י וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ הַיָּשָׁ֤ר בְּעֵינַי֙ לִשְׁמ֤וֹר חֻקּוֹתַי֙ וּמִצְוֺתַ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֑י וְהָיִ֣יתִי עִמָּ֗ךְ וּבָנִ֨יתִי לְךָ֤ בַֽיִת־נֶאֱמָן֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנִ֣יתִי לְדָוִ֔ד וְנָתַתִּ֥י לְךָ֖ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And it shall be, if you listen to all that I command you, and walk in my ways, and do the right in my eyes, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as did David my servant, and I will be with you and build for you a house enduring as I built for David, and I will give to you Israel.

en.L: And it shall be, if you listen to all that I command you, and walk in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ways, and do what [is] right in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes, keeping {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments, as David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave did, then I will be with you, and I will build for you an enduring house, as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.
en.B: If you heed all that I command you, follow {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ways, and do what is right in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight by keeping {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments, as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David did, I will be with you. I will build you an enduring house, as I did for David, and I will make Israel yours.
en.R: If you obey everything I command you, live the way I want you to live, and do what I say is right by keeping {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and commands, as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David did. If you do, I will be with you. I will give you a family line of kings that will last, as I did for David. I will give Israel to you.

decisions.choice: an enduring house: the promise once made to David
decisions.reason: The same words were spoken to David through Nathan: "your house ... will be made sure" (2 Samuel 7:16; 1 Samuel 25:28). A house here is a royal family, a line of kings.

decisions.choice: if you listen: an offer with a condition
decisions.reason: Jeroboam is offered what David received, on the same terms of loyalty to Yahweh. Whether his house lasts will depend on how he lives (14:7-11).

decisions.choice: my slave (Literal); my servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

decisions.choice: a family line of kings that will last
decisions.reason: Readable says what "house" means here (m1).

source.text: וַֽאעַנֶּ֛ה אֶת־זֶ֥רַע דָּוִ֖ד לְמַ֣עַן זֹ֑את אַ֖ךְ לֹ֥א כָל־הַיָּמִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will afflict [the] seed of David because of this, but not all the days.

en.L: And I will afflict the seed of David because of this, but not all the days.'"
en.B: Because of this I will humble David's descendants, but not forever.'"
en.R: Because of what Solomon has done, I will humble David's descendants, but not forever.'"

decisions.choice: afflict: humble, bring low
decisions.reason: The verb means to press down or humble. David's line will be brought low by the loss of most of its kingdom.

decisions.choice: but not all the days: the humbling of David's line will end
decisions.reason: The judgment has a limit. The promise to David stands, and the prophets look ahead to a son of David who will reign again over all Israel (Isaiah 9:6; Ezekiel 37:22-24; Amos 9:11).

decisions.choice: the verse is in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The main manuscripts of the ancient Greek translation do not have this verse. The Hebrew, followed here, has it.

decisions.choice: what Solomon has done
decisions.reason: Readable says what "this" refers to: Solomon's worship of other gods (verse 33).

source.text: וַיְבַקֵּ֥שׁ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְהָמִ֣ית אֶת־יָרָבְעָ֑ם וַיָּ֣קָם יָרָבְעָ֗ם וַיִּבְרַ֤ח מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ אֶל־שִׁישַׁ֣ק מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיְהִ֥י בְמִצְרַ֖יִם עַד־מ֥וֹת שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And sought Solomon to put to death Jeroboam; and arose Jeroboam and fled [to] Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and he was in Egypt until [the] death of Solomon.

en.L: And Solomon sought to put Jeroboam to death, but Jeroboam arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and he was in Egypt until the death of Solomon.
en.B: Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and stayed there until Solomon died.
en.R: So Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam. But Jeroboam escaped to Egypt, to King Shishak, and stayed there until Solomon died.

decisions.choice: Shishak: the pharaoh Sheshonq I
decisions.reason: Shishak is the first pharaoh named in Kings. He later invaded Judah in the fifth year of Rehoboam (14:25-26).

decisions.choice: fled to Egypt: like Hadad
decisions.reason: Jeroboam, like Hadad (verse 17), escapes to Egypt and waits there for the king's death before returning (12:2).

decisions.choice: Solomon sought to put him to death: because of the rebellion
decisions.reason: The account does not say how Solomon learned of the prophecy, but Jeroboam had already "lifted up a hand against the king" (verse 26).

source.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֧י שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה וְחָכְמָת֑וֹ הֲלֽוֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתֻבִ֔ים עַל־סֵ֖פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of Solomon?

en.L: And the rest of the matters of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the matters of Solomon?
en.B: The rest of the acts of Solomon, all that he did and his wisdom, are written in the Book of the Acts of Solomon.
en.R: Everything else Solomon did, and his wisdom, is written in the history of Solomon.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of Solomon: a written record of his reign
decisions.reason: This is the first time Kings points to its sources. The writer names a book that recorded Solomon's reign and sends the reader to it for more. Later notices name the records of the kings of Israel and of Judah (14:19, 29). These books have not survived.

decisions.choice: matters: deeds, events, and words
decisions.reason: The word means "words" or "matters": what was said and done. "The matters of Solomon" are the events of his reign.

decisions.choice: are they not written?: a question that means "they are written"
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes. It is the usual way Kings closes a reign.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of Solomon / the Book of the Acts of Solomon / the history of Solomon
decisions.reason: This follows the wording kept for the source formula in these books (the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel / the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel / the history of the kings of Israel), adapted to a book about one king. Here the Hebrew has no "days", so Balanced says "Acts", as in "the rest of the acts".

decisions.choice: are written
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the answer the question expects (m3); Literal keeps the question.

source.text: וְהַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר֩ מָלַ֨ךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה בִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the days which reigned Solomon in Jerusalem over all Israel [were] forty years.

en.L: And the days that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel [were] forty years.
en.B: Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.
en.R: Solomon ruled over all Israel from Jerusalem for forty years.

decisions.choice: forty years: the length of a generation
decisions.reason: David also reigned forty years (2:11). Forty is a common round number for a generation, and the figure may be rounded.

decisions.choice: all Israel: the whole united kingdom
decisions.reason: Solomon is the last king to rule over all twelve tribes. After him the kingdom divides (chapter 12).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב שְׁלֹמֹה֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּ֨קָּבֵ֔ר בְּעִ֖יר דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ רְחַבְעָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And lay down Solomon with his fathers, and he was buried in [the] city of David his father; and reigned Rehoboam his son in his place.

en.L: And Solomon lay down with his fathers and was buried in the City of David his father, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.
en.B: Then Solomon rested with his ancestors and was buried in the City of David his father. And his son Rehoboam became king in his place.
en.R: Then Solomon died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David, his father's city. His son Rehoboam became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The formula Kings uses for the death of a king, as at 2:10.

decisions.choice: the City of David: the old part of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As at 2:10, the City of David was the stronghold David took from the Jebusites, where the kings of Judah were buried.

decisions.choice: Rehoboam his son: the next king
decisions.reason: Rehoboam's mother was Naamah, an Ammonite (14:21). His reign begins with the division the prophet foretold (chapter 12).

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula is worded the same way at each level throughout Kings. Readable adds "with his ancestors" where the burial is named, as the terms for these books ask.
